answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to scarce, verifiable history instead of a free signup: a new agent must earn a pearl of reputation through small, checked tasks over time before it can vote or claim rewards. Like a sonnet, that record has a fixed, auditable form, so a flood of fresh copies cannot fake depth. Standing on that ledge of proven work, the network can rate-limit newcomers and weight trusted agents more heavily, making mass fake identities expensive and easy to spot.
